title: Can a ball go through a wall? With 80% of the energy needed, never. 3.2% of a quantum wave gets out.
description:
Can a ball go through a wall? Top: a ball with 80% of the energy it needs to get over a wall, rolled at the wall. Bottom: a quantum wave packet with exactly the same energy sent at the same wall. The wave is the Schrodinger equation solved step by step (split-step Fourier, Strang splitting), the ball is plain mechanics. Natural units, no seed.

Measured:
- the ball hits the near face of the wall at 13.96 s of video and bounces back; it never passes, 0%
- the wave packet: mean energy 80.05% of the wall height; at the end of the run 96.823% of it is reflected, 0.0002% is still inside the wall, and 3.177% is past the wall on the far side; total probability 1.0000000000
- the transmitted share reaches half its final value at 16.2 s of video and 99% of it at 25.5 s
- checks: 3.161% at half the time step, 3.176% on twice the grid (65,536 points against 32,768); the digit the checks agree on, 3.2%, is the one in the narration
- closed form for a single-energy wave at 80% of the wall: 3.000% (the packet carries a spread of energies, and transmission grows faster than linearly with energy, so the packet's 3.18% sits above it)
- half the wall width: 26.02% gets through, 8.2 times more; twice the wall width: 0.0734%, 43 times less
- the share of the packet's momentum components with enough energy to top the wall classically: 0.0002%, so the 3.2% is not the fast tail of the packet climbing over

Setup: wave number k0 = 1, width sigma = 20, start x = -80, kinetic energy 0.5; wall height 0.625 and width 4.44 (kappa a = 2.22); grid of 32,768 points with the wall tiling exactly 180 cells; 2,400 frames of 8 steps of dt = 0.0104 to t = 200; 5 time units per second of video.

On screen the wave panel draws the amplitude of the wave (the square root of the probability density), so the small transmitted part is visible; the readout counts probability, the share of the wave past the wall.

The Schrodinger equation is 100 years old this year (1926).

Rerun sims/tunnel/tunnel.py with projects/tunnel/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.

Made end to end by an AI agent: simulation, footage, voice, music, and edit.
